lessons.rationale: When multiple sequences represent corresponding fields of the same records, transforming one sequence independently can silently destroy those relationships. The failed behavior sorted keys but left values in their original positions, producing valid-looking output with incorrect associations. Pair records first, then sort or transform the records as units; test with deliberately non-monotonic inputs so positional mismatches are exposed.
lessons.summary: Preserve relationships between parallel data by bundling corresponding elements before reordering.
lessons.when: Use this principle whenever sorting, filtering, grouping, or otherwise reordering one of several correlated sequences.

lessons.rationale: A generator or iterator is stateful: consuming it once advances it to exhaustion, so later operations such as sum(stream) may see no items and produce an incorrect result. Materialize a single-use iterable once, then compute every required statistic from that stable snapshot. After applying the repair, inspect the actual source and rerun tests, because a reported patch or intermediate success may not reflect the file ultimately under test.
lessons.summary: When multiple calculations depend on an iterable that may be single-use, consume it exactly once into a reusable collection and derive all calculations from that collection.
lessons.when: Use this whenever code needs to count, sum, validate, partition, or otherwise make multiple passes over an input that could be a generator or iterator.

lessons.rationale: A failing cache lookup can come from either an incorrect key or an incorrect key-generation contract. Before replacing a helper with a direct tuple or primitive, trace how inputs flow into the stored key and inspect whether the helper is an intentional extension point. A repair should separate all required identity dimensions while preserving any documented normalization or override behavior.
lessons.summary: When fixing cache collisions, correct the key’s identity dimensions without bypassing the component’s key-generation abstraction.
lessons.when: When a cache, memoization table, or lookup map reuses results across calls that should be independent, inspect both the complete key and the helper or hook that constructs it before editing the lookup logic.

lesson_origin.selection_rule: All families whose first development triplet met the original accuracy or 15-percent model-call signal rule; all three selected lessons supplied in every lesson arm.
